content.title: Celtics-Sixers recap: Tatum, C's dominate Sixers in Game 1 rout
content.text: Boston CelticsLive Blog EndedApr 19, 2026 The Celtics hardly broke a sweat in their 123-91 victory. NBC Universal, Inc. Chris Forsberg, Eddie House and Tom Giles break down the Celtics’ Game 1 win over the Sixers on Postgame Live What to KnowChris Forsberg and Kayla Burton shared more postgame reaction on the Celtics Talk Podcast.Jaylen Brown dropped a game-high 26 points, including 16 in the third quarter.Jayson Tatum logged 25 points, 11 rebounds, seven assists, and two steals.Celtics shot 36.4 percent (16-44) from 3; Sixers shot 17.4 percent (4-23) from deep.Game 2 is set for 7 p.m. ET Tuesday at TD Garden. BOSTON -- The Boston Celtics treated the TD Garden crowd to a lopsided 123-91 Game 1 win over the Philadelphia 76ers on Sunday. Boston never trailed in the victory. Jaylen Brown (26 points) and Jayson Tatum (25 points) led the way in the masterful performance. Tatum added 11 rebounds, seven assists, and two steals. The C's shot 50 percent from the floor (16-44 3-PT), while the Sixers shot 39 percent from the field (4-23 3-PT). Game 2 at TD Garden is scheduled for Tuesday at 7 p.m. ET. Check out our live blog below for a full recap of Game 1: BOSTON -- It was a dominant performance from start to finish for the Celtics as they took down the Philadelphia 76ers in Game 1 of their first-round series, 123-91. Jayson Tatum set the tone with 10 first-quarter points and kept his foot on the gas, finishing with 25 points on 9-of-17 shooting from the field. The Celtics superstar also logged 11 rebounds, seven assists, and two steals in what was an outstanding all-around showing in his first playoff game since his Achilles injury. Jaylen Brown added a game-high 26 points (11-21 FG, including 16 points in third quarter) and four rebounds, while Neemias Queta notched 13 points. Derrick White chipped in 10 points and six assists. Sam Hauser drilled four 3s to finish with 12 points, and Payton Pritchard scored 12 with six assists off the bench. The Sixers in Game 1 when Jayson Tatum was primary defender, per NBA tracking: 6-19 FG (31.6 percent), two steals Maxey when defended by Tatum in Game 1: 1-5 FG, two points Twenty-five points, 11 rebounds, seven assists and that defense from a "still rehabbing" Tatum. The C's fans at TD Garden mocked Sixers fans' "We want Boston" chants while Boston cruised to a blowout Game 1 win. Jayson Tatum shared his reaction: “I heard it. I mean, we have a tremendous crowd," Tatum said. "Obviously, missing 60 some-odd games, I missed playing in front of our own crowd. Just the opportunity to play here in the playoffs is special and something I’ll never take for granted." In the first quarter, Sam Hauser took a charge from Adem Bona. He hadn't taken a charge throughout the regular season. After the game, he shared his reacton: "I was scared," he quipped. "That's a big dude." Sunday's game marked the first playoff appearance for a handful of Celtics players. Jaylen Brown shared what he told the young group before taking the court: "Just breathe. Manage your emotions," Brown said. "They might go on a run, they might not go on a run, but just stay together. Win the fight. Be the harder-playing team and guard. Don't save yourself for offense; our offense is going to be fine if we guard. That was my message." Celtics star Jayson Tatum put on a show in his first playoff game since last year's Achilles injury. After Sunday's win, he reflected on his return to playoff basketball in Boston: "I understand the magnitude of the injury and the narrative around me coming back and everything in between," he said. "I'm proud of what I've been able to accomplish and return to play and all those things. There were many of days where I wasn't even sure I was going to play this season, let alone get a chance to play today." Tatum also spoke about rebuilding his confidence on his road to recovery. "The day that it changed or became a real thought is when I got assigned to the G League and we had the scrimmage. That was really the first time that I was like, 'I might come back this year.'" The Celtics' 32-point win in Game 1 is the largest margin of victory in a playoff opener in franchise history. Jaylen Brown spoke on the team's preparation and setting the tone with a dominant performance. "We're ready. We're prepared," Brown said. "We just gotta be ready every time we step out on the floor, but great tone-setter. A lot of great teams have played in a Celtics uniform. For us to have the biggest margin of victory in (a playoff opener) is great. It sets the tone and it reflects our focus and our intensity." Boston's previous largest margin of victory in a playoff opener was 23 vs. the Atlanta Hawks in 2008. Celtics big man Neemias Queta spoke with NBC Sports Boston's Abby Chin after the Game 1 victory and heaped praise on teammates Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown. "They're the head of the snake for us," he told Chin Watch the full interview below: Abby Chin caught up with Neemias Queta after the C's dominant Game 1 win over Philly Eddie House and our Celtics Postgame Live crew react to Boston dominating Philly in Game 1, 123-91. Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla appreciated the passion from the fans at TD Garden after they mocked Sixers fans' "We Want Boston" chants. He noted that C's fans helped set the tone for the team's dominant performance. “I thought our fans were great tonight, helped us get off to a good start," Mazzulla said. "Playoff basketball obviously means more, and it's different in Boston. Which we appreciate.” After his exceptional Game 1 performance, Jayson Tatum spoke to ESPN about returning to the playoffs after last year's devastating Achilles injury. "Today was probably the most excited, and relaxed, and grateful I've been in my nine years of being in the playoffs," Tatum said. Chants of "We Want Boston" were heard in Philadelphia's Xfinity Mobile Arena on Wednesday as the Sixers secured a win over the Magic that set up a first-round matchup with the Celtics. Philly fans got what they wished for. Near the end of Sunday's blowout victory at TD Garden, Celtics fans mocked Sixers fans with a "We Want Boston" chant of their own: Score: 120-91 Celtics, 1:01 left in fourth quarter With this game just about in the books, Joe Mazzulla has emptied the bench. That means Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum's days are over after dropping 26 and 25 points, respectively. Ron Harper Jr. quickly drilled a 3 for the first playoff points of his career. Score: 105-75 Celtics, 9:16 left in fourth quarter Barring a stunning collapse, this one is all but over. The Celtics have extended their lead to 30 points with a 10-4 run to begin the fourth. Sam Hauser started the frame with back-to-back 3s. Score: 95-71 Celtics The C's are 12 minutes away from a lopsided Game 1 win. They've outclassed the Sixers in nearly every facet of the game, especially 3-point shooting. They're 11-of-29 (38 percent) from deep while Philly is just 3-of-20 (15 percent). Jaylen Brown dropped 16 of his team-leading 26 points in the third quarter. He's shooting 11-of-21 from the field. Score: 79-58 Celtics, 5:55 left in third quarter The C's were a bit sluggish to start the second half, but they've since gotten their groove back to jump out to a 21-point lead over the Sixers. Jaylen Brown (15 points) and Nikola Vucevic (three points) hit back-to-back 3-pointers just before the timeout. Derrick White also made a 3 earlier in the quarter. Jayson Tatum still leads Boston with 21 points, while Paul George leads Philly with 15. Jayson Tatum became the third NBA player in the play-by-play era to log at least 21 points, eight rebounds, four assists, and two steals in the first half of a playoff game, joining Jimmy Butler and Russell Westbrook, per Celtics stats guru Dick Lipe. Score: 64-46 Celtics The Celtics showed for most of the first half why they're the heavy favorites in this series. They outshot the Sixers 50 percent to 33 percent from the field and 33 percent (6-18) to 13 percent (2-16) from 3-point range. One area Boston would like to improve in the second half: offensive rebounding. Philly dominated the offensive glass, 10-3. Jayson Tatum was the star of the half for the C's, logging 21 points (7-11 FG) with eight rebounds and four assists. Jaylen Brown chipped in 10 points and four rebounds. Score: 56-36 Celtics, 2:47 left in second quarter This has been a one-sided game so far, with the C's dominating throughout the first half. They're shooting 52 percent from the floor (6-15 3-PT) while the Sixers are just 29 percent from the field (2-15 3-PT). Jayson Tatum has been outstanding. He leads the Celtics with 13 points (6-9 FG), eight rebounds, and four assists. Score: 49-31 Celtics, 6:50 left in second quarter Jaylen Brown scored four quick points in the second quarter after scoring four in the entire first. It's been a rocky start for the C's star, but he has looked sharper so far in this frame. Luka Garza came off the Celtics bench and recorded five points, including a 3. He also committed two fouls, joining the list of big men in this game in early foul trouble. Neemias Queta, Nikola Vucevic, Adem Bona, and Andre Drummond each have two fouls. Jayson Tatum is only the third player in the play-by-play era to have at least 10 points, seven rebounds, and four assists in the first quarter of a playoff game, per Celtics stats guru Dick Lipe. Score: 33-18 Celtics The Celtics' playoff run began with a dominant first quarter against the Sixers. Jayson Tatum did a bit of everything for the C's in the opening frame with 10 points, seven rebounds, four assists, and a steal. He shot 5-of-7 from the floor in his first playoff game since last year's Achilles injury. Sam Hauser hit a pair of 3s early to set the tone for Boston. Jaylen Brown had four points before being subbed out for Jordan Walsh, who closed the quarter with a bucket on a Tatum assist. Payton Pritchard added five points off the bench. Score: 24-14 Celtics, 2:39 left in first quarter The Sixers have had their chances to take control early in this game, but they haven't been able to get their open looks to fall. They're just 1-for-7 from deep so far, while the C's are 3-for-6. Jayson Tatum and Sam Hauser lead the Celtics with six points apiece. Jaylen Brown had four before being subbed out for Jordan Walsh. Derrick White made his first 3 of the postseason. The big men on both sides are in early foul trouble. Neemias Queta, Nikola Vucevic, Adem Bona, and Andre Drummond each have two fouls. Tyrese Maxey (nine points) and Paul George (five points) have scored all of Philly's points so far. Score: 15-7 Celtics, 7:24 left in first quarter The Celtics have jumped out to an early eight-point lead with two Sam Hauser 3-pointers, plus buckets from Jayson Tatum (four points, 2-3 FG). Tatum also already has three assists and two rebounds. Boston has forced four Philly turnovers. Tatum, Jaylen Brown (two points), and Derrick White each have steals. Nikola Vucevic is the first big man off the C's bench to replace Neemias Queta (three points), who has two early fouls. Sixers big man Adem Bona also has two fouls and was replaced early by Andre Drummond. On Celtics Pregame Live, C's owner Bill Chisholm shared two hilarious stories about coach Joe Mazzulla. "I'm hearing stories about that he voluntarily got himself tased over the summer," Chsholm said. ... "He entered an MMA tournament with his wife's maiden name... and then he won." Mazzulla has openly stated that he "hates" the NBA Coach of the Year award, but Chisholm said he's going to have to get over it. "Sorry, Joe, you're Coach of the Year. Suck it up." Bill and Kimberly Chisholm join Celtics Pregame Live to share a few hilarious Joe Mazzulla stories. Celtics: Derrick White, Jaylen Brown, Sam Hauser, Jayson Tatum, Neemias Queta Sixers: Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Kelly Oubre, Paul George, Adem Bona The Celtics and 76ers met four times during the regular season, splitting their series 2-2. Boston didn't have superstar Jayson Tatum for any of those matchups, however. Before Sunday's Game, Sixers coach Nick Nurse spoke about the challenge of facing the C's with Tatum back in the lineup: "We played against him a lot over the years. Obviously he's a great player that makes them better," Nurse said. "Just one more thing you have to worry about." Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla spoke before Game 1 about how his team is approaching another playoff run: “Our messaging internally has been the same however long I’ve been in the Celtics organization," he said. "Just have to be consistent in the things that impact winning and understand that there's highs, there's lows. If you stay consistent to the process of winning, and stick together, the results take care of itself." Jaylen Brown showed up early to TD Garden in preparation for the C's first-round clash with the Sixers: Brian Scalabrine breaks down what makes the Celtics’ player development team different than others in the league. Ask an NBA fan about Payton Pritchard, and chances are they'll bring up the 2024 NBA Finals, when the Celtics guard buried halfcourt buzzer-beaters in Game 2 and Game 5 to help Boston dispatch the Dallas Mavericks and raise Banner 18. Those two heaves were undoubtedly Pritchard's most famous shot clock beaters. But they certainly weren't his last. Over the last two regular seasons since that Finals victory, Pritchard has scored a whopping 307 points on 132 made field goals in "late shot clock" situations, which the NBA defines as zero to four seconds on the 24-second timer. In 2025-26 alone, Pritchard poured in 203 points on 89 for 204 shooting (43.6 percent) in late shot clock situations, leading the entire NBA in all three categories. One of the NBA's greatest rivalries resumes Sunday when the Boston Celtics host the Philadelphia 76ers in Game 1 of their first-round playoff series. It will be the 23rd playoff series between these longtime Eastern Conference foes. The Celtics have won the last six playoff series in this rivalry dating back to the 1985 Eastern Conference Finals. They are heavy favorites in this upcoming matchup, too. The C's exceeded all expectations this season. Despite losing several key players (Kristaps Porzingis, Jrue Holiday, Al Horford, etc.) in the offseason, and not having Jayson Tatum until March as he recovered from an Achilles injury, the Celtics earned the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference. Read Full ArticleWe take a deeper look inside the Celtics’ player development system and examine how they’ve sustained such consistent success over the years The Boston Celtics' 2025-26 season finale was an ode to the organization's exceptional player development program. Boston's "Stay Ready" culture was on full display in its 113-108 win over the Orlando Magic. The C's sat eight rotation players, including all five starters, but still put on a show against a fully healthy Magic squad. Baylor Scheierman, drafted at the end of the first round in 2024, led the way with a career-high 30 points. Ron Harper Jr., who couldn't get minutes with Toronto or Detroit, erupted for 27 points just days after having his two-way contract converted to a standard NBA deal. Luka Garza added 27 points and 12 rebounds to wrap up a standout campaign after failing to carve out a consistent role in Minnesota. The B Team's big night wasn't a huge surprise to anyone who has followed the Celtics closely in recent years. Boston's bench unit is nicknamed the "Stay Ready Group" for a reason. Read Full ArticleJaylen Brown talks gearing up for the playoffs after accomplishing more than many people expected this season. For the 24th time in NBA history and the sixth time this century, the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers will meet in the playoffs. The storied rivals will face off in the first round, marking the first Boston-Philly playoff matchup since the 2023 Eastern Conference semifinals when the C's defeated the Sixers in seven games. This year, the Celtics earned the No. 2 seed with a 56-26 record, while the Sixers secured the No. 7 seed with a 45-37 record and a win over the Orlando Magic in the No. 7 vs. No. 8 play-in tournament matchup on Wednesday night. Boston and Philadelphia played four times in the regular season, splitting their series 2-2. The C's were without Jayson Tatum for all four matchups due to his Achilles injury, but the superstar is healthy and looking like himself just in time for the postseason. As for the Sixers, star big man Joel Embiid's status remains up in the air after he underwent an emergency appendectomy. If he's out, Philly will lean heavily on Tyrese Maxey and Paul George to carry the load. Read Full ArticleJaylen Brown talks “historic run” with Jayson Tatum and the Celtics. The 2025-26 NBA regular season is in the rearview mirror, and the Boston Celtics outkicked most outsider expectations as part of their 56-win season. With a long ramp to Sunday’s Game 1 of a first-round series, it felt like a good time to both revisit our seven bold preseason predictions and deliver a fresh batch of seven predictions for the postseason trek ahead. Here is how our crystal ball fared with our seven bold preseason predictions: 1. Jaylen Brown returns to an All-NBA team. We don’t even need to wait for the voting. It’s a lock. Read Full ArticleAbby Chin caught up with Sam Hauser after the Celtics dominated the Pelicans 144-118 and clinched the No. 2 seed. The Boston Celtics' 2025-26 regular season has come to an end. But before we turn our attention to the team's quest for Banner 19, it's time to recognize the C's who played key roles en route to the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference. From MVP (an obvious choice) to the biggest surprise (a toss-up), we handed out superlatives and awards for a team that smashed preseason expectations. Here's who's taking home the fake hardware: No need to spend much time on this no-brainer. Jaylen Brown was counted on to step up as the Celtics' No. 1 option with Jayson Tatum out, and he exceeded even the loftiest expectations. In what many believed would be a "gap year" for the C's, Brown averaged career highs in points (28.7), rebounds (6.9), and assists (5.1) per game while leading Boston to a 56-26 record and the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference. Read Full ArticleOur Postgame Live crew reacts to the Celtics’ incredible win over the Orlando Magic. Superstar players are essential to winning an NBA title, perhaps more than in any other major North American sports league. But role players still can make a huge difference on the road to a championship. Role players have the ability to swing a game in your favor, and sometimes even an entire series. Celtics playoff history is full of examples. Glenn McDonald played a pivotal role in the triple-overtime Game 5 classic against the Phoenix Suns in the 1976 NBA Finals. Leon Powe dominated the Lakers with 21 points in Game 2 of the 2008 NBA Finals. James Posey hit a couple huge 3-pointers in Boston's historic comeback win over the Lakers in Game 4 of the 2008 Finals. Sam Hauser shot 47.8 percent on 3-pointers in the 2024 NBA Finals win over the Mavericks. Read Full ArticleChris Forsberg and Kayla Burton break down Joe Mazzulla’s case for Coach of the Year, and what he might do if he gets it. Is the whole "gap year" narrative surrounding the Boston Celtics a bit overblown? Perhaps. But there's a reason why national and local media alike predicted a steep drop-off for the C's this season. Boston lost a total of 8,749 minutes and 4,415 points -- 46 percent of its total scoring output -- from its 2024-25 squad over the offseason. Its best player, Jayson Tatum, was sidelined due to a ruptured Achilles, while four core contributors -- Kristaps Porzingis, Jrue Holiday, Al Horford and Luke Kornet -- departed via trade or free agency, replaced by the likes of Anfernee Simons, Luka Garza, Josh Minott and rookie Hugo Gonzalez. And yet... Joe Mazzulla's squad hardly missed a step. The 2025-26 Celtics enter the postseason as the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference -- the same seed as last year -- and their 56-26 regular-season record was just five wins off last season's pace of 61-21. That's a remarkable achievement, especially when you consider Tatum played in just 16 games after making his season debut on March 6. President of basketball operations Brad Stevens also traded away four players ahead of the NBA trade deadline in February -- Anfernee Simons, Josh Minott, Chris Boucher and Xavier Tillman Sr. -- leaving the Celtics to lean more heavily on Jaylen Brown, Derrick White, Payton Pritchard and Sam Hauser while giving expanded roles to young players such as Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh.
